name: Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program — Medical Care Regardless of Immigration Status
description: The Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program is the largest federally funded program in the United States dedicated to improving healthcare access for people living with HIV who are uninsured or underinsured. Crucially, the program does not use immigration status when determining eligibility for services funded by its grants, making it one of the few federal health programs accessible to undocumented immigrants, those within the Medicaid five-year waiting period, and refugees or asylees who have lost time-limited benefits. Services include outpatient and ambulatory medical care, prescription medications through the AIDS Drug Assistance Program (ADAP), dental care, mental health services, substance abuse treatment, medical case management, and medical transportation. The program funds over 2,200 community-based organizations, clinics, and health departments across all 50 states and U.S. territories. For immigrant communities disproportionately affected by HIV, this program provides a critical safety net when other federal and state programs are inaccessible due to immigration status restrictions.
eligibility: People living with HIV/AIDS who are uninsured, underinsured, or lack sufficient healthcare coverage; no immigration status requirement — open to undocumented immigrants, asylum seekers, refugees, visa holders, and lawful permanent residents; must meet income eligibility thresholds set by local grantees (typically at or below 300-500% of the federal poverty level)
amount: Free medical services — no direct cash grants to individuals; services funded through grants to community organizations
applicationProcess: Contact your nearest Ryan White-funded clinic or community organization. Use the HRSA Health Center Finder at findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov or call 1-800-275-4772 to locate a provider. Walk in or call to schedule an intake appointment. Staff will assess your eligibility based on income and HIV status. No Social Security number or proof of immigration status is required to receive services. You will be connected to a medical case manager who will coordinate your care plan.
geographicScope: United States — all 50 states, District of Columbia, U.S. territories, and freely associated jurisdictions
documentsRequired: Proof of HIV-positive status (lab results or medical records), proof of income (pay stubs, tax returns, or self-attestation), photo identification (any form accepted by the local provider); immigration documents are NOT required

name: NYC Care — Free Primary and Preventive Healthcare for All New Yorkers
description: NYC Care is a healthcare access program operated by NYC Health + Hospitals, the largest public healthcare system in the United States, that guarantees low-cost and no-cost healthcare services to New Yorkers who cannot afford or are ineligible for health insurance — including undocumented immigrants. The program provides a primary care provider, access to specialty care, prescription medications at reduced rates, mental health services, and preventive care such as screenings and vaccinations. Members receive a membership card and a dedicated 24/7 customer service line with multilingual support. NYC Care serves as a critical healthcare bridge for immigrants who are excluded from Medicaid, the ACA marketplace, and employer-sponsored insurance due to their immigration status. The program operates through NYC Health + Hospitals' 70+ patient care locations across all five boroughs, including 11 acute-care hospitals, five post-acute care facilities, and more than 50 community health centers.
eligibility: New York City residents who are ineligible for or cannot afford health insurance; no immigration status requirement — open to undocumented immigrants, asylum seekers, and all New Yorkers regardless of documentation; must live in one of the five boroughs of New York City; income typically at or below 200% of the federal poverty level for free services, sliding scale available for higher incomes
amount: Free or low-cost — primary care visits, specialty care, prescription medications, and preventive services at no or reduced cost based on income
applicationProcess: Call 1-646-NYC-CARE (1-646-692-2273) to enroll by phone with multilingual support available, or visit any NYC Health + Hospitals location to enroll in person. You can also enroll online at nyccare.nyc. Provide basic personal and income information. No Social Security number or immigration documents required. Once enrolled, you will be assigned a primary care provider and receive a membership card. Services are available immediately upon enrollment.
geographicScope: New York City — all five boroughs (Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, Bronx, Staten Island)
documentsRequired: Proof of New York City residency (utility bill, lease, mail with NYC address), proof of income (pay stubs or self-attestation), photo identification (any form accepted, including consular ID or foreign passport); NO immigration documents required

name: California Full-Scope Medi-Cal for All Adults Regardless of Immigration Status
organization: California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS)
description: California became the first state in the United States to offer full-scope Medicaid coverage (Medi-Cal) to all income-eligible adults regardless of immigration status. Effective January 1, 2024, all Californians aged 26–49 who meet income requirements became eligible, completing the state's phased expansion that began with children in 2016 and extended to young adults (19–25) in 2020 and adults 50+ in 2022. Full-scope Medi-Cal provides comprehensive healthcare including doctor visits, hospital care, prescription drugs, dental care, vision services, mental health treatment, substance use disorder services, and long-term care. This program is particularly significant for undocumented immigrants who are excluded from federal Medicaid and ACA marketplace coverage. California funds this expansion entirely with state dollars, making it the most comprehensive immigrant health coverage program in the nation. Over 700,000 additional undocumented adults became eligible through the final expansion phase.
eligibility: California residents of any age who meet Medi-Cal income requirements (generally up to 138% of the federal poverty level for adults); no immigration status requirement — open to undocumented immigrants, DACA recipients, asylum seekers, visa holders, and all California residents regardless of documentation; must be a California resident
amount: Free comprehensive healthcare coverage — doctor visits, hospital care, prescriptions, dental, vision, mental health, and more at no cost to eligible individuals
applicationProcess: Apply online at CoveredCA.com or BenefitsCal.com, by phone at 1-800-541-5555, in person at your county social services office, or through a certified enrollment counselor. Complete the Medi-Cal application with household income and residency information. No Social Security number is required for the applicant (an SSN is requested but applicants may decline). Applications are processed by the county and coverage begins retroactively to the month of application upon approval.
documentsRequired: Proof of California residency (utility bill, lease, mail with California address), proof of income (pay stubs, tax returns, or self-attestation), proof of identity (any photo ID accepted including foreign passport or consular ID); immigration documents are NOT required for the immigrant expansion population

name: Illinois Health Benefits for Immigrant Adults (HBIA)
organization: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
description: The Illinois Health Benefits for Immigrant Adults (HBIA) program provides comprehensive Medicaid-equivalent healthcare coverage to immigrant adults aged 42 and older who reside in Illinois and are not eligible for federal Medicaid due to their immigration status. Illinois was among the first states to extend full healthcare coverage to older undocumented adults, recognizing that this population faces disproportionate health challenges and has the fewest healthcare options. The program covers a full range of medical services including primary care, specialist visits, hospital care, prescription medications, mental health services, dental care, vision services, and long-term care. Combined with the state's existing coverage for immigrant children (All Kids) and younger adults through separate programs, Illinois provides one of the most comprehensive safety nets for immigrant health in the United States. The program is funded entirely by the state of Illinois.
eligibility: Illinois residents aged 42 and older who are not eligible for federal Medicaid due to immigration status; must meet Medicaid income requirements (generally up to 138% of the federal poverty level); must be an Illinois resident; no specific immigration status required — open to undocumented immigrants and other non-citizens ineligible for federal programs
amount: Free comprehensive healthcare coverage — doctor visits, hospital care, prescriptions, dental, vision, mental health, and long-term care at no cost to eligible individuals
applicationProcess: Apply online at ABE.illinois.gov (Application for Benefits Eligibility), by phone at 1-800-226-0768, or in person at a local Department of Human Services (DHS) office. Complete the application with household income, residency, and basic personal information. A caseworker will review the application and determine eligibility. Coverage begins upon approval and is renewable annually. Multilingual assistance is available.
documentsRequired: Proof of Illinois residency (utility bill, lease, or mail with Illinois address), proof of age (birth certificate, passport, or other official document), proof of income (pay stubs, tax returns, or self-attestation), photo identification (any form accepted); immigration documents are NOT required

name: Penn Orphan Disease Center — Million Dollar Bike Ride Pilot Grants
organization: Orphan Disease Center, University of Pennsylvania
description: The University of Pennsylvania's Orphan Disease Center (ODC) administers the Million Dollar Bike Ride Pilot Grant Program, which funds translational research projects for rare and orphan diseases. Each year, the program awards pilot grants of up to $50,000 per project to researchers worldwide who are investigating new treatments, diagnostics, or disease mechanisms for rare conditions. The grants are open to the international community — any faculty-level researcher at an academic institution or senior scientist at a non-profit organization or foundation may apply, regardless of country. This makes the program particularly valuable for international researchers and for patients with rare diseases who cross borders seeking treatment and participation in cutting-edge research. Since its inception, the program has funded over 200 research projects across dozens of rare diseases, many of which have led to larger funded studies, new clinical trials, and drug development programs. Research areas span genetics, gene therapy, pharmacology, biomarker development, and natural history studies.
eligibility: Faculty-level researchers at academic institutions or senior scientists at non-profit organizations and foundations worldwide; projects must focus on rare or orphan diseases; open to international applicants regardless of country of origin; must align with one of the rare disease areas supported by the Bike Ride fundraising teams
amount: Up to $50,000 per pilot grant project
targetDiagnosis: Rare and orphan diseases (various — aligned with specific Bike Ride fundraising teams)
applicationProcess: Visit the Orphan Disease Center website at orphandiseasecenter.med.upenn.edu/grants for the current call for proposals. Review the list of eligible rare disease areas supported by the current year's Bike Ride teams. Submit a research proposal including specific aims, significance, innovation, approach, budget, and biosketches. Applications are peer-reviewed and grants are awarded annually following the Million Dollar Bike Ride event. Check the website for current cycle deadlines.
documentsRequired: Research proposal with specific aims, detailed budget and justification, NIH-format biosketches for key personnel, letter of support from institution, proof of faculty or senior scientist appointment
